architecture.mechanism: Active aerodynamic shape adaptation reduces pressure drag by delaying flow separation and controlling the wake at high speed, while a low-drag baseline body and hybrid powertrain reduce parasitic and engine losses.
architecture.intervention: A teardrop-inspired low-drag body with active rear spoiler and underbody diffuser that deploy above 80 mph, plus a small turbocharged engine coupled to a motor-generator and low-rolling-resistance narrow tires.
architecture.expected_effect: Drag coefficient below 0.20 with spoiler deployed, enabling 200 mph with under 150 hp and fuel consumption below 40 mpg at 200 mph or below 3 L/100 km in a standardized high-speed cycle.
architecture.falsification_test: Build a 1/4-scale clay or 3D-printed model with a servo-actuated spoiler and test in a university wind tunnel at 80–120 mph equivalent Reynolds number; if drag reduction is under 10% or wake pressure recovery is unchanged, the active aero hypothesis fails.
